# Lock and pop-out never reach a dock workspace that configures nothing

## Context

Operator ruling 2026-09-03: a dock workspace that configures nothing must project the full header action rail — "lock => GOAL was neo default true", "popout MUST BE THERE BY DEFAULT".

Measured on a downstream workspace that overrides none of the six `enableDock*Action` flags (headless Chromium against the running app, action nodes read per header): focusing a center-owned pane yields `[maximize, close]`; focusing an edge-owned pane yields `[unpin, maximize, close]`. Lock and pop-out never appear.

Both absences are **correct against currently accepted ACs**. That is what this ticket revises — it is a successor to two deliberate decisions, not a defect report against them.

## The Problem

**1. Lock.** #18014 AC-1 reads: "… and retain explicit `false` opt-out; `enableDockLockAction` remains default-off." The action itself shipped complete under #17949 (`fa-lock` ↔ `fa-lock-open`, aria lock/unlock, focus-gated while unlocked and persistent while locked) and #18044 added per-pane delegation (`dockLock(locked)`) — but no default consumer renders it. The consequence was named on 2026-09-01: default-off plus no Workstation opt-in means the operator "has not felt it by hand", with a proposed opt-in step that never executed.

**2. Pop-out.** #17947 AC-1 witnessed a DOUBLE gate as correct: "Default off: byte-identical projection. On without `enableDockTearOutLifecycle`: still byte-identical (double gate witnessed)." The consequence is that `enableDockPopOutAction` defaults `true` while being **structurally unsatisfiable**: `dockPopOutActionActive` = `enableDockPopOutAction === true && !!this.tearOutHandlers`, and handlers are composed only under `enableDockTearOutLifecycle`, which defaults `false`. A host reads an enabled flag, gets no action, and receives no runtime signal.

Pop-out is the sharper half. An enabled flag that can never render is a workspace-wide constant falsehood, not per-item variance — and `enableDockTearOutLifecycle`'s own JSDoc frames its default as temporary: "Disabled by default so ordinary workspaces and hosts carrying their own legacy lifecycle remain byte-behaviorally unchanged **until their migration leaf**." This is that leaf.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:145` — `enableDockLockAction: false`; `:215` — `enableDockPopOutAction: true`; `:266` — `enableDockTearOutLifecycle: false`.
- `Workspace#dockPopOutActionActive` is the single effective predicate ("Two questions must never disagree"), passed to the adapter as `dockPopOutActionAvailable`.
- `src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs:1113` builds `headerActions`: lock enters only under `context.enableDockLockAction`; pop-out enters under `enableDockPopOutAction` but with `hidden: !activeItemId || !context.dockPopOutActionAvailable`.
- A withdrawn focus-gated action carries **no DOM node** (#18015), so an absent action is indistinguishable from a disabled flag by inspection. That is why this went unnoticed by eye.

## The Fix

1. `enableDockLockAction` defaults `true`; explicit `false` retained as the opt-out. Amends #18014 AC-1.
2. Pop-out becomes available to a default workspace. Two candidate shapes:
   - **(a)** `enableDockTearOutLifecycle` defaults `true` — the migration leaf its JSDoc anticipates. Moves tear-out lifecycle ownership for every existing host that carries its own.
   - **(b)** Decouple availability from the legacy-lifecycle flag: the engine composes its own `tearOutHandlers` when a host supplies none, leaving `enableDockTearOutLifecycle` as the opt-in for hosts that want the engine to own the WHOLE lifecycle.
   
   **(b) is the recommendation** — it makes the enabled flag honest without moving lifecycle ownership under any host that already has one.
3. Whichever shape lands: an enabled action that cannot render must not be silently inert. A dev-mode warning names the action and the missing capability.

| `Workspace#enableDockTearOutLifecycle` | `:266` | unchanged under (b); `true` under (a) | hosts with their own lifecycle keep it | JSDoc | byte-identical projection arm for existing hosts |

## Decision Record impact

`amends ADR 0029` — the docking design record's tear-out lifecycle and default-posture rows. Also amends the accepted ACs of #18014 (AC-1) and #17947 (AC-1); both tickets are CLOSED with merged PRs, so this is a successor, never a reopen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace` subclass that overrides nothing projects `lock` at the frozen slot; explicit `enableDockLockAction: false` still removes it.
- [ ] AC-2 The same bare workspace projects a `pop-out` that is reachable (not `hidden`) on a focused item, with the host supplying no `tearOutHandlers`.
- [ ] AC-3 Existing hosts carrying their own tear-out lifecycle keep byte-identical projection and exactly one lifecycle owner — no second handler, listener or vessel owner (the invariant #17947 AC-1 and #18014 AC-9 protect).
- [ ] AC-4 An enabled action that cannot render logs one dev-mode warning naming the action and the missing capability; production stays silent.
- [ ] AC-5 A red-first witness asserts the DEFAULT action vector for a bare workspace and is red at the current head. Absence is asserted as **node presence**, not display (#18015).
- [ ] AC-6 The frozen order `lock · reload · pin · pop-out · maximize · close` is unchanged; close stays persistent and last.
- [ ] AC-7 Exact-head unit + component suites green; the lock and pop-out arms mutation-proven.

## Out of Scope

- Reload's default availability — its own successor, filed alongside this one.
- Pin's edge-ownership gate: **verified working** (present on an edge-owned pane, withheld on a center-owned one). A consumer layout concern, not an engine one.
- The locked-pane presentation design pass — #18044 shipped delegation; the gray-out question stays open.

## Avoided Traps

- **Flipping `enableDockTearOutLifecycle` to `true` as the obvious one-line fix.** Its default-false is load-bearing for hosts carrying a legacy lifecycle, and #18014 AC-9 requires exactly one lifecycle owner. A one-line flip moves ownership under those hosts silently — the reason (b) is recommended over (a).
- **Reading an absent DOM node as a disabled flag.** Withdrawn actions carry no node, so presence is the only honest instrument. A grep for these flags across a consumer tree returns nothing precisely *because* they are already `true`.

## Related

- #18014 (closed) — AC-1 set the default vector and kept lock off; this amends it.
- #17947 (closed) — AC-1 witnessed the pop-out double gate; this amends it.
- #17949 (closed) — the lock action itself. #18044 (closed) — per-pane `dockLock` delegation.
- #18015 — withdrawn actions have zero extent and no node.
- ADR 0029 — docking design record.

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-02T22:55:49Z

Closing as **superseded by #18151**, on the operator's direction and my own re-read.

This ticket described lock and pop-out as two wrong defaults. They are two instances of one defect, and filing them as defaults framed the symptom: the dock's extension hooks answer "decline" by default, so a consumer that writes none of them gets slower, incomplete behaviour with no signal. `getRefreshOptions` → `{}`, `resolveFreshPane` → `null`, `openTearOutVessel` → `null`. The engine owns the operation vocabulary and the persisted item records; asking a consumer to re-derive that knowledge is the layering error, and flipping individual defaults would have left it in place.

Two corrections to what this ticket asserted, both measured after filing:

- **AC-2 was wrong as written.** It asked that a bare workspace "projects a `pop-out` that is reachable (not `hidden`)". Reachable-but-dead satisfies that literally, and that is exactly what shipping it produced: enabling `enableDockTearOutLifecycle` renders the action and a click opens nothing, because `openTearOutVessel` returns `null` in the base class. Driven on a real consumer: one action node, zero windows opened, the pane still in the main window, no error. An AC for an action must assert the effect, never the affordance.
- **There is nothing for a consumer to inherit.** `createVesselOwnerGrant` / `revokeVesselOwnerGrant` / `lastVesselOpen` / `tearOutVesselDims` are all app-local to `apps/workstation`, not engine members. A consumer wiring pop-out today implements the opener, the retirement seam, and the vessel-side adoption — three implementations, not a flag.

The evidence from this ticket is carried into #18151's problem scope, including the #18014 AC-1 and #17947 AC-1 anchors showing both defaults were accepted, witnessed decisions rather than oversights. Nothing here is lost; the shape is better one level up.

— Vega (Opus 5, Claude Code) 🌿
